Duration::ceil¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Duration Duration::ceil(std::string_view unit) const;

Advance To A Unit Boundary¶

ceil() replaces every elapsed value with the smallest exact multiple of unit that is not less than that value. Exact multiples remain unchanged. This is fixed-width elapsed-time rounding: a day is exactly 86,400 seconds and a week is exactly seven such days. No calendar, timezone, or daylight-saving rule participates.

The accepted unit spellings are "ns", "us", "ms", "s", "min", "h", "D", and "W". They are deliberately canonical and case-sensitive; descriptive alternatives such as "second" are rejected rather than guessed.

The operation allocates a new Duration, preserves rank and shape, and leaves NaT lanes unchanged. Negative values still obey the mathematical ceiling: -1.6 s and -1.5 s both become -1 s, moving toward positive infinity.

Examples¶

Example 1. Positive and negative values advance independently to seconds.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos({
    -1'600'000'000LL, -1'500'000'000LL, -500'000'000LL,
     500'000'000LL,  1'500'000'000LL, 2'500'000'000LL,
     1'400'000'000LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT,
});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.ceil("s").total().nanoseconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.0000e+09, -1.0000e+09, 0.0000e+00, 1.0000e+09, 2.0000e+09, 3.0000e+09, 2.0000e+09, nan]

Example 2. A matrix keeps its shape; only its lanes change.

auto matrix = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {1, 1'000'000'000, 1'000'000'001, pluss::Duration::kNaT}, {2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::duration::print(matrix.ceil("s"));

The results are 1 s, 1 s, 2 s, and NaT, arranged in the original [2,2] shape. An exact boundary is not advanced a second time.

Example 3. Invalid units and unrepresentable rounded values fail before a partial result is returned.

pluss::duration::seconds(1).ceil("second"); // throws: Duration: unsupported unit

pluss::duration::nanos((std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max)())
    .ceil("D");                              // throws: Duration rounding overflow

See Also¶

  • floor(): move to the boundary at or below each value.

  • round(): choose the nearest boundary with half-even ties.
